preamble: Change of airstream from glottalic egressive (ejective) to glottalic ingressive (implosive): [tʼ] becomes voiced [ɗ]. Where Highland East Cushitic has tʼ, Oromo and Arbore have the implosive ɗ; in Konso and Gidole ɗ reflects *tʼ only before i(i)C (Ehret 1991: 246, after Arvanites), and Burji has palatalized cʼ before front vowels; Sasse (1979) reconstructs *ɗ instead, so the direction is disputed. The two sounds share glottal closure, and Omotic Chara varies jaltʼa ~ jalɗa 'crooked', while Tzʼutujil /tʼ/ can be realized as [ɗ] (Dayley 1985), showing the phonetic proximity.
